item.title: HDOCK-Multimer: improved structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating docking and combinatorial assembly
item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01062-1

This study presents HDOCK-Multimer, a general framework for structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating ab initio docking and combinatorial assembly, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art methods.

item.title: HIP: Hessian Interatomic Potentials without derivatives
item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01066-x

The authors introduce an extension of machine learning interatomic potentials that predicts molecular Hessians directly, improving accuracy and speed compared in transition-state searches, geometry optimization and vibrational analysis relative to Hessians from automatic differentiation.

item.title: LLMs predict material properties based on atom types and not atom positions
item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01044-3

Accurately predicting properties of materials is one of the main challenges in computational materials science. Systematic experiments now show that large language models (LLMs) struggle to use positional information for the prediction of those properties. This limitation does not reverse as model or dataset sizes grow.
item.dc:title: LLMs predict material properties based on atom types and not atom positions
